rv.q: In Wicker Park, Shelley has pulled off something notable, in service of the resilience of the country of her birth and of what remains possible in Chicago theater if an audience is willing to take a risk.

The problem is that Cesaire’s 1963 play (translated from the French by Paul Breslin and Rachel Ney and adapted for the House by artistic director Lanise Antoine Shelley) seems intended to be studied more than performed.
This is theater at its finest and I highly recommend that you see it.
The Tragedy of King Christophe lacks precisely that sort of propulsive story, and no amount of directorial creativity or actorly skill can make up for its absence.

cn.t: Mixed reviews greet this House Theatre production of Césaire's historical drama about Haiti's first king. Critics praise the committed ensemble and fascinating subject matter, but fault the play itself for prioritizing political discourse over compelling characters.
